recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Revisit only if the Terminology Infrastructure WG creates a new decision to add an enforceable invariant for cases where sourceScope or targetScope do not imply a single system.
issue_request: FHIR-14710 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification STU3 ConceptMap request to make ConceptMap.group.source and ConceptMap.group.target mandatory so source and target code systems would always be known. The final resolution allowed group.source and group.target to be omitted when source or target value sets identify only one system, and preserved optional root source/target scope elements for empty $closure initiation.
initial_application: The issue appears to have been applied in svn r14010, preserved as git commit 7a03cbd98d, which updated the old ConceptMap spreadsheet comments to say group.source and group.target are not needed when the corresponding value set is specified and contains concepts from only a single system. The related earlier FHIR-12314 closure decision had already relaxed old root ConceptMap.source[x] and ConceptMap.target[x] cardinalities from 1..1 to 0..1.
additional_context: ConceptMap is active in the current build through source/fhir.ini, and source/conceptmap/structuredefinition-ConceptMap.xml is the authoritative current source. Later work renamed ConceptMap.source[x] and ConceptMap.target[x] to sourceScope[x] and targetScope[x] and added usage notes for value-set mappings, but did not reverse the 2018 cardinality outcome. The referenced Zulip thread records implementer input, the $closure use case, and the conclusion to document the rule rather than tighten cardinalities.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current source keeps sourceScope[x], targetScope[x], group.source, and group.target at 0..1, and the group.source/group.target comments already state the single-system value-set exception approved by FHIR-14710.
